answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task or claim a reward. The protocol caps each stake’s influence and slashes it when a randomly audited claim is proven fraudulent, so one operator cannot cheaply multiply influence by minting identities. A legitimate newcomer can wander in and build a record, while a sybil attacker must lock real capital across accounts and risk losing it; a pearl of code or a mirror identity cannot substitute for that cost.
